title: 1985 Mexico City Earthquake
summary: On the morning of 19 September 1985 an earthquake of about magnitude 8 struck the subduction zone off Michoacan, on Mexico's Pacific coast. The worst damage came about 220 miles away in Mexico City, whose soft lake-bed ground prolonged the shaking. NIST gives 10,000 deaths and 3,000 buildings demolished; Berkeley notes official death tolls range from 9,500 to 35,000.

uncertainty.note: Sources agree on the date; local time given as 7:18 (NIST) or 7:19 (Berkeley) am. Magnitude given as 8.1 by both.

where.modern_name: Mexico City, Mexico (pin is the city, a proxy for the damage zone; the epicentre was offshore Michoacan, not pinned)

importance.justification: One of the deadliest earthquakes in the Americas, showing how lake-bed soil can amplify distant shaking.

audience_note: Describes a disaster with thousands of deaths, including people trapped in collapsed buildings.

reviewer_note: Magnitude (8.0 vs 8.1) and deaths vary by source; the pin is Mexico City, not the epicentre, as no opened page gave epicentre coordinates.
